title: EvalCatalog
description: Vocabulary of the per-draft EvalResult evals (HAR-97 §3-§6, §9, §15(GTM)) and of the offline-benchmark situations (§20): per eval type its kind, single evidence class, labels, blocking rule and HAR-97 sections; HAR-97 evals that produce no EvalResult on a draft are listed in out_of_scope. The instance is contracts/evals/eval_catalog.json; completeness (every evalType present) is tested.

out_of_scope.description: HAR-97 evals deliberately not modelled as an EvalResult on a draft, with the reason and where they are measured instead.

contract.description: The contract schema that records this eval's outcome instead of an EvalResult.

case_types.description: Situations the offline benchmark must deliberately test (HAR-97 §20), with a one-line description.

labels.description: Allowed categorical labels; [] means the eval's label is always null.

sections.description: HAR-97 sections: '§4', '§5.14', '§15(GTM).3' (the GTM-grounded '# 15.', not '# 15. Demo story'), '§16(DEMO)' (not '# 16. Runs UI'), '§5(PITCH)' (the '# 5.' of the 'Core demo pitch' at the top of HAR-97, whose §1-§11 collide with the later headings), an eval layer L1-L5, or a named unnumbered heading.

gtmEvidenceClass.description: The evidence classes HAR-97 §15(GTM) names for GTM practice; semantic evals use one of them.

evidence_class.description: The ONE class that supports this eval as GTM practice; every judgment of this type carries it.

status.description: planned: the type is in the vocabulary (so results, tables and wording can name it) but no judge emits it yet. Absent means shipped.

can_block.description: false: a judgment of this type is never blocking.

label_rule.description: How to choose between labels where more than one could fit.

allOf.description: A semantic eval always states its blocking rule (never-blocks or when-it-blocks); the judges read blocking from the catalog only (HAR-116).
Semantic evals carry a GTM evidence class (HAR-114, HAR-97 §15(GTM)); product_rule is for deterministic, trace and human-delta evals.
A type that may block cannot state a never-blocks rule.
